changes: No substantive changes. Notes now cover the uncertain bracketed word ⁅pratya⁆karo, the reading of dvijātmanā, and the date check.

date.as_written: abde lakṣmaṇasenasa〇mmate(!) śatacatuṣṭaye caturvviṃśatau ca likhyamāne | pauṣe py asite pakṣe ’māvāsyānvite ravau

notes: The date is written out in words: śatacatuṣṭaye caturviṃśatau = 424 in the Lakṣmaṇasena era (LS). Using the LS+1119 conversion this is about 1543 CE, but the LS epoch is disputed, so the CE year is approximate. The catalogue's 'pauṣa 30' matches amāvāsyā (new-moon day) of the dark half. Jayadeva is a brahmin (vipra) of Kaṅkapura, the village where the copy was made. His role depends on the uncertain bracketed word ⁅pratya⁆karo. It could perhaps be a corrupt pratyakṣakara, 'one who examined/witnessed', or some patron-like function. Commissioner, owner or corrector cannot be confirmed, so he is entered as 'other'. dvijātmanā is read as 'by the twice-born (brahmin) Rāma'. It could also mean 'son of a brahmin', but no father is named.
